text:
alex: Heads-up: I'm proposing we reduce default retention for non-privileged auth logs from 365d -> 90d to cut storage/cost and reduce blast radius. Paired with that: timeboxed transient snapshots for vuln triage and a JIT KMS unwrap flow. Need opinions on RBAC + export implications.

mira: Quick q — any legal or compliance blockers? some regulators expect longer auth logs for investigations.

alex: Good call. Checked with legal last week — baseline for most product accounts is fine at 90d. We need an exemption process for regulated customers and an emergency legal-hold path.

jin: If we shorten retention, how do SIEM exports behave? Downstream partners might expect older data for analytics.

alex: Plan is: SIEM streaming/alerts keep real-time indices as now. For exports to partners we will emit a retention-copy when the export is requested, but only with an approval ticket and CMK-wrap. Exports will be time-limited and logged.

sam: RBAC idea: introduce two scoped roles — `security_snapshot_reader` (read-only, timebound) and `triage_elevate` (can request snapshots). Requests require approver from SecOps or on-call.

katie: For KMS unwrap we should use a proxy that mints ephemeral unwrap tokens (ttl short). That avoids granting long-lived kms:Decrypt to many principals. Example request flow below: 
```
POST /kms-proxy/unwrap 
{
  "snapshot_id": "snap-20260321-09",
  "approver": "sec-lead",
  "justification": "vuln-triage-#4321",
  "ttl_secs": 7200
}
```
Proxy returns a short-lived unwrap token tied to the request id.

opsbot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/789 (retention + snapshoting RFC) :paperclip:

mira: We must audit every unwrap event. Log principal, request id, approver, ttl, and query fingerprint. Those audit logs must be retained longer (2y) — investigators need the unwrap trail.

alex: Agreed. Add a new audit stream `kms_unwrap_audit` with 2y retention and high-fidelity fields. We'll also push those to the forensic bucket on legal-hold.

jin: Operational question — will reducing retention affect alerting rules that rely on trend detection over 6+ months?

alex: We will keep aggregated metrics (counts, baselines) for 12 months in the metrics store (not raw logs). Long-term behavioral models can use those aggregates. Raw logs older than 90d go to an encrypted cold archive (customer-specific CMK) if needed for deep analytics.

sam: Emergency/legal hold process: we should implement a ticket that copies relevant partitions to `legal-hold` bucket with separate CMK and retention policy (7y). This should bypass the normal lifecycle and require sec+legal signoff.

katie: +1 on legal-hold bucket. Also suggest a small CLI for triage: `redwood sec snapshot create --scope auth --duration 120m --justification "vuln-1234"` that wires approval flow.

alex: Draft plan I will put in the RFC:
- Change default auth_log lifecycle to 90d
- Add `security_snapshot_reader` & `triage_elevate` roles (timeboxed)
- Implement KMS-proxy ephemeral unwrap tokens + `kms_unwrap_audit` stream (2y retention)
- SIEM exports require approval + CMK-wrap, export copies are time-limited
- Legal-hold ticket to copy to `legal-hold` bucket (7y retention)

mira: sounds sensible. can you add a matrix of who can approve and SLOs for snapshot creation (target <5min for triage)?

alex: will add. tagging @sam @katie for RBAC + KMS proxy review.

mira: :thumbsup:

sam: I can review the RBAC patch tomorrow morning.

katie: I'll prototype the KMS-proxy unwrap endpoint this week and link a demo in the PR.

alex: Thanks everyone — I'll update the RFC and send a short review meeting invite.
